items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Ever since then I noticed -- I saw a film with John Faddis... [INTERVIEWEE] Well, that's amazing. I don't see how he could do that.

ctx.x: No, because this is -- the trumpet is usually right on the tip of the center of your lip. And that means the muscles have to develop on either side to keep the air from going out, and that was my trouble. When I got to blow a trumpet, air was coming out on both corners of my lips.
Ever since then I noticed -- I saw a film with John Faddis, you know, Dizzy's disciple, and when he was blowing, to the left of his mouth
Well, that's amazing. I don't see how he could do that.
